name: Lydian weight-standard electrum coinage
description: In Lydia, makers produced electrum pieces with struck marks and standardized weights that functioned as coins.

impact.note: Struck coinage descended from it through Greek, Persian and Roman mints to most of the world, reorganising exchange and founding minting and monetary practice.

date.label: About 650 BCE
date.basis: The museum dates its representative coins to about 650 BCE.

events.statement: Lydian electrum coins were produced to weight standards and marked with designs.
events.scope: The museum dates representative coins; this is not a proven date of invention.

evidence.supports: Lydian electrum coins were produced to weight standards and marked with designs.

earliest_record.rationale: Date and scope follow the cited event; this is the earliest episode established in this research, not a claim of world priority.

caveats: The reasons for issue and the issuing authority are uncertain; the museum infers a royal connection from a lion symbol. No global-first or uniform acceptance claim is made.

research.note: Independent second reader checked the cited historical episodes, dates and actor roles against the stated source passages, subject to the caveats; other facets are not blanket reviewed.
